1.2 Read the data

I worked with a training data set (data) to explore trends and fit models and a test dataset (test_genera) to test the models’ performance

Training data

data=read.csv('damage_data_core_genera.csv')
data_w = pivot_wider(data[,-c(3:4)],
           names_from = tool_param,
           values_from = value )
data_w$mapdamage_1_over_lambda=1/data_w$mapdamage_lambda
data_w$pydamage_1over_p=1/data_w$pydamage_p
data_w$qPCRcopies_per_uL_and_mg_rock=data_w$qPCRcopies_per_uL/data_w$mass_mg

Test data

test_genera = read_csv("damage_data_test_genera.csv")
## Rows: 4482 Columns: 20
## ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Delimiter: ","
## chr  (8): sample, genus, tool, variable, sample_name, dft_interval, Library,...
## dbl (12): value, min_age_yrs_bf_1950, max_age_yrs_bf_1950, mean_age_yrs_bf_1...
## 
## ℹ Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## ℹ Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
test_genera_w = pivot_wider(test_genera[,-c(3:4)],
           names_from = tool_param,
           values_from = value )
test_genera_w$qPCRcopies_per_uL_and_mg_rock=test_genera_w$qPCRcopies_per_uL/test_genera_w$mass_mg

2. Plot functions

plot_saturation_curves=function(table, param){
  ggplot(table, aes(x = median_age_yrs_bf_1950)) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(x = median_age_yrs_bf_1950, ymin = CI_lower_full, ymax = CI_upper_full), alpha=0.1, fill = "darkred") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(x = median_age_yrs_bf_1950, ymin = CI_lower_trunc, ymax = CI_upper_trunc), alpha=0.1, fill = "black") +
  geom_line(aes(y= CI_lower_full), color="darkred", linetype='dotted')+
  geom_line(aes(y= CI_upper_full), color="darkred", linetype='dotted')+
   geom_line(aes(y= CI_lower_trunc), color="black", linetype='dotted')+
  geom_line(aes(y= CI_upper_trunc), color="black", linetype='dotted')+
  geom_point(aes(y = {{param}}), shape = 4, color='gray60', size=1) +
  geom_line(aes(y=fitted_full), color='darkred',linetype='solid')+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 32000, color='gray40')+
  geom_line( aes(y = fitted_trunc), color = "black",linetype='solid')+
  theme_bw(base_size=9)+
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0), limits=c(0,38000))+
  labs(x = "Nominal Age (Years BP)")
}
plot_residuals=function(table){
ggplot(table)+
geom_point(aes(x=median_age_yrs_bf_1950, y=residual_full),shape=1,color="darkred", size=2)+
geom_point(aes(x=median_age_yrs_bf_1950, y=residual_trunc),shape=16, color="black", size=1)+
geom_hline(yintercept=0)+
geom_vline(xintercept=32000,color='gray40')+
geom_segment(aes(x = median_age_yrs_bf_1950, y = residual_full, xend = median_age_yrs_bf_1950, yend = residual_trunc))+
theme_bw(base_size = 9)+
labs(x='Nominal Age (Years BP)', y='Residual')
}

3. Exponential saturation models: Damage over time

3.1 delta_s over time

3.1.1 Fit

plottable_delta_s=data_w[,c('median_age_yrs_bf_1950', 'mapdamage_delta_s', 'genus','sample','gc_gc')]
fit_delta_s_trunc <- nls(mapdamage_delta_s  ~ 1 - exp(-r * median_age_yrs_bf_1950),data = plottable_delta_s[plottable_delta_s$median_age_yrs_bf_1950<32000,],start = list(r = 1e-3))
summary(fit_delta_s_trunc)
## 
## Formula: mapdamage_delta_s ~ 1 - exp(-r * median_age_yrs_bf_1950)
## 
## Parameters:
##    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## r 1.503e-03  3.596e-05   41.78   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.03187 on 312 degrees of freedom
## 
## Number of iterations to convergence: 6 
## Achieved convergence tolerance: 8.924e-07
fit_delta_s_full <- nls(mapdamage_delta_s  ~ 1 - exp(-r * median_age_yrs_bf_1950),data = plottable_delta_s,start = list(r = 1e-3))
 summary(fit_delta_s_full)
## 
## Formula: mapdamage_delta_s ~ 1 - exp(-r * median_age_yrs_bf_1950)
## 
## Parameters:
##    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## r 1.503e-03  3.484e-05   43.13   <2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.03088 on 340 degrees of freedom
## 
## Number of iterations to convergence: 6 
## Achieved convergence tolerance: 8.824e-07

3.1.2 Confidence and Prediction interval

# Prediction intervals
#full data
CI_delta_s_full <- predictNLS(fit_delta_s_full,
                     newdata =data.frame(median_age_yrs_bf_1950=plottable_delta_s$median_age_yrs_bf_1950),interval = "confidence",alpha = 0.05,nsim = 10000)$summary
#truncated data
CI_delta_s_trunc <- predictNLS(fit_delta_s_trunc,
                     newdata =data.frame(median_age_yrs_bf_1950=plottable_delta_s$median_age_yrs_bf_1950),interval = "confidence",alpha = 0.05,nsim = 10000)$summary

3.1.3 Plot

plottable_delta_s$CI_lower_full <- CI_delta_s_full[, "Sim.2.5%"]
plottable_delta_s$CI_upper_full <- CI_delta_s_full[, "Sim.97.5%"]
plottable_delta_s$fitted_full <- predict(fit_delta_s_full)
plottable_delta_s$residual_full=residuals(fit_delta_s_full)

plottable_delta_s$CI_lower_trunc <- CI_delta_s_trunc[, "Sim.2.5%"]
plottable_delta_s$CI_upper_trunc <- CI_delta_s_trunc[, "Sim.97.5%"]
plottable_delta_s$fitted_trunc = predict(fit_delta_s_trunc, newdata = plottable_delta_s)
plottable_delta_s$residual_trunc= plottable_delta_s$mapdamage_delta_s - predict(fit_delta_s_trunc, newdata = plottable_delta_s)
p_deltas=plot_saturation_curves(plottable_delta_s, mapdamage_delta_s)
p_deltas

3.1.5 Residuals

delta_s_res=plot_residuals(plottable_delta_s)

delta_s_res

3.2 pmax over time

3.2.1 Fit

plottable_pmax=data_w[,c('median_age_yrs_bf_1950', 'pydamage_pmax','genus', 'sample', 'gc_gc')]
# Fit the model using nls
fit_pmax_full <- nls(pydamage_pmax  ~ a+b * (1 - exp(-r * median_age_yrs_bf_1950)),
data = plottable_pmax,
start = list(r = 1e-4, b=0.6,a=0.2))
summary(fit_pmax_full)
## 
## Formula: pydamage_pmax ~ a + b * (1 - exp(-r * median_age_yrs_bf_1950))

## Parameters:
##    Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)

fit_pmax_trunc <- nls(pydamage_pmax  ~ a+b * (1 - exp(-r * median_age_yrs_bf_1950)),

3.4 length mode over time

3.4.1 Fit

plottable_mode <- data_w[,c('median_age_yrs_bf_1950', 'compute_length_mode', 'genus', 'sample', 'gc_gc')]
fit_mode_full <- nls(
compute_length_mode ~ Lmin + (L0 - Lmin) * exp(-lambda * median_age_yrs_bf_1950),
data = plottable_mode,
start = list(L0 = 70, Lmin = 30, lambda = 0.0001))

summary(fit_mode_full)
## 
## Formula: compute_length_mode ~ Lmin + (L0 - Lmin) * exp(-lambda * median_age_yrs_bf_1950)

## 
## Residual standard error: 7.061 on 338 degrees of freedom

4.2.1 bootstrapping confidence band

bootstrap_pairwise_by_genus_sample <- function(
  data,
  time_col = "median_age_yrs_bf_1950",
  damage_col = "pydamage_pmax",
  sample_col = "sample",
  genus_col = "genus",
  R = 100,
  seed = 1963) {
  set.seed(seed)
 #construct pairs from data
  all_pairs <- data %>%
    rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_i")) %>%
    crossing(
      data %>% rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_j"))
    ) %>%
    filter(!!sym(paste0(sample_col, "_i")) != !!sym(paste0(sample_col, "_j"))) %>%
    mutate(delta_pmax = !!sym(paste0(damage_col, "_j")) - !!sym(paste0(damage_col, "_i")))
#define range of delta_pmax  
  delta_seq <- seq(
    min(all_pairs$delta_pmax),
    max(all_pairs$delta_pmax),
    length.out = 100)
  # Precompute unique levels and their row indices
  genus_levels = unique(data[[genus_col]])
  sample_levels = unique(data[[sample_col]])
  genus_index_list = lapply(genus_levels, function(g) which(data[[genus_col]]  == g))
  sample_index_list = lapply(sample_levels, function(s) which(data[[sample_col]] == s))
  # Container for predictions
  pred_matrix <- matrix(NA, nrow = R, ncol = length(delta_seq))
  for (r in seq_len(R)) {
    ## 1) Resample genus *clusters* by index, with replacement
    g_ids = sample(seq_along(genus_levels),
                    size = length(genus_levels),
                    replace = TRUE)
    ## 2) Resample sample *clusters* by index, with replacement
    s_ids = sample(seq_along(sample_levels),
                    size = length(sample_levels),
                    replace = TRUE)
    ## 3) Get the row indices for the resampled clusters
    rows_g = unlist(genus_index_list[g_ids])
    rows_s = unlist(sample_index_list[s_ids])
    ## 4) Intersection: rows that belong to both a resampled genus and sample
    rows_keep = intersect(rows_g, rows_s)
    d_resample = data[rows_keep, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(d_resample) < 2) {
      next  # skip iteration if not enough data
    }
    #build pairs and fit glm based on resampled data
    pairs = d_resample %>%
      rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_i")) %>%
      tidyr::crossing(
        d_resample %>% rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_j"))
      ) %>%
      dplyr::filter(.data[[paste0(sample_col, "_i")]] != .data[[paste0(sample_col, "_j")]]) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        delta_pmax = .data[[paste0(damage_col, "_j")]] -.data[[paste0(damage_col, "_i")]],
        y_ij = as.integer(.data[[paste0(time_col, "_j")]] >.data[[paste0(time_col, "_i")]]))
    if (nrow(pairs) == 0) {
      next}
    mod = glm(y_ij ~ delta_pmax, family = binomial(), data = pairs)
    pred_matrix[r, ] = predict(mod,newdata = data.frame(delta_pmax = delta_seq),type = "response") }
# Compute 95% CI from pred_matrix
ci = apply(pred_matrix, 2, function(x) quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE))
ci_df = data.frame(
  delta_pmax = delta_seq,
  lwr = ci[1, ],
  upr = ci[2, ],
  fit = apply(pred_matrix, 2, mean, na.rm = TRUE))
# Return complete results
list(bootstrap_predictions = pred_matrix,ci_df = ci_df)}
result_two_way = bootstrap_pairwise_by_genus_sample(data = data_w[data_w$median_age_yrs_bf_1950<32000,] ,R = 500)

4.2.2 Plot

plottable_logit=result_two_way$ci_df %>% mutate(orig_pred = predict(pmax_logit, 
                    newdata = data.frame(delta_pmax = .$delta_pmax), 
                    type = "response"))
find_cutoff_crossing <- function(df, p) {
  df %>%
    filter(orig_pred >= p | lwr >= p | upr >= p) %>%
    summarise(
      prob = p,
      delta_pmax_fit = min(delta_pmax[orig_pred >= p], na.rm = TRUE),
      delta_pmax_lwr = min(delta_pmax[lwr >= p], na.rm = TRUE),
      delta_pmax_upr = min(delta_pmax[upr >= p], na.rm = TRUE)
    )
}

cut_095 <- find_cutoff_crossing(plottable_logit, 0.95)
cut_075 <- find_cutoff_crossing(plottable_logit, 0.75)

bind_rows(cut_095, cut_075)

4.3.2 Classification threshold

coords(roc_obj, "best", ret = c("threshold","sensitivity", "specificity"), best.method="youden")
qlogis(c(0.5)) / coef(pmax_logit)['delta_pmax']
## delta_pmax 
##          0

0.5 is the most suited threshold for class separation, this corresponds to a delta_pmax of 0 (as expected for logit model)

pairs_test$pred_class <- pairs_test$pred_prob > 0.5
table(

  pred  = pairs_test$pred_class

4.3.3 Binned data approach

pairs_test_plot <- pairs_test %>%
  mutate( correct = as.integer((delta_pmax > 0) == (median_age_yrs_bf_1950_j>median_age_yrs_bf_1950_i)), abs_dp = abs(delta_pmax),
      dp_bin = cut_width(abs_dp, width = 0.025, boundary = 0),include.lowest = TRUE)%>% 
 mutate(correct = factor(correct, levels = c(0, 1),
                     labels = c("Incorrect", "Correct"))) %>% 
  group_by(dp_bin, correct) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(dp_bin) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n))
bars=ggplot(pairs_test_plot, aes(x = dp_bin, y = prop, fill = correct)) +

  ) +
